text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- The government plans to stop public programme of combination vaccines, including an anti-diptheria serum, due to rising prices.

- Former Transport and Art Minister Rudolf Scholten is a possible candidate to become the new chief executive of Creditanstalt after its takeover by Bank Austria. Bank Austria chief Danilo Melamed is also likely to become a board member of Creditanstalt.
- Grocery chain Julius Meinl's pre-tax profits jumped to more than 100 million schillings in 1996 from 19 million schillings the year before.
- The Chamber of Economy favours the idea of giving 60,000 legally resident foreigners a work permit and says this would not endanger the Austrian job market.
DIE PRESSE
- The reform of Austria's trading regulations is the centre of heated debate between trade organisations.
- Austria's banks have agreed to make rate changes for private loans more transparent.
- Post & Telekom Austria board member Walther Richter wants to reintegrate the mobile phone company Mobilkom. However, other board members have harshly criticised this idea.
- First talks on further austerity budgets for 1998 and 1999 will start today. However, an increase of public pensions for 1998 is already planned.
- Banks have yet to decide on a 600-million-schilling claim reduction for sports goods maker HTM, so the company still has no balance sheet for 1995.
- Investmentbank Austria sees potential for a 20 percent rise in the share price of steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm.
KURIER
- Austrian government revenues are two billion schillings higher so far this year than in 1996, as budget talks start today.
- Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger will start talks on the reform of private pension plans.
- Hannes Androsch's investment group's planned export figures for salt monopoly Salinen AG, which it wants to takeover in a joint bid with Raiffeisenbank, are doubted.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Social Democrats want to strengthen federal grid company Verbund by vetoing the liberalisation plans of conservative Economics Minister Hannes Farnleitner.
- Trading of Verbund shares at the New York stock exchange will soon start as the bourse's supervisory board has admitted the company.
